items.title: ChatGPT ships an Apple Messages plug-in that can read and send texts for you
items.summary: OpenAI released a plug-in on August 20 that connects ChatGPT to a Mac's iMessage, SMS, and RCS threads, letting it search message history, draft replies, and send texts on the user's behalf. It's Apple Silicon-only and lives inside Codex/ChatGPT Work rather than ordinary chats; OpenAI keeps a default confirmation step before any message goes out and explicitly warns against enabling persistent auto-approval.
items.whyItMatters: The default-on confirm-before-send gate (and OpenAI's explicit warning against disabling it) is a reusable UX pattern worth copying if Romain or Anna ever take real-world actions on a learner's behalf, like sending a progress recap or scheduling a review session.

items.title: Survey data: public trust in AI keeps sliding despite the tech getting better
items.summary: Reported August 19, Pew Research finds 52% of Americans are now "more concerned than excited" about AI in daily life, up from 37% in 2021, and an Economist/YouGov poll shows over 70% think AI is advancing too fast. The gap: people aren't feeling tangible personal benefit yet, and worry about job loss, even as industry leaders admit promised applications (like healthcare) haven't materialized.
items.whyItMatters: A consumer-facing tutor selling to everyday learners, not developers, is selling into this exact trust gap; leading with concrete, felt benefits (visible progress, not 'powered by AI') matters more than the model story.
